resources.string: Queued behind another game\'s Prepare: it starts by itself.
%1$s is no longer in the library. Nothing in it was deleted.
%1$s games are listed but not playable yet: their console comes in a later version.
Too many files: the scan of a folder stopped at 5,000 entries
Choose your library folders: the folders where your disc images, game folders and game files are (one per console, say).
No game found in the library folders yet.
In your library folder. Import it once to play: its files are copied into the app.
This folder can only be read through Android\'s file picker: it must be copied into the app to be played.
The app lost its access to the library folder. Choose it again.
Its folder is no longer in the library folder.
Its pack was built from another version of the game, or the game refused it: prepare it again.
Taken out of the Prepare queue.
%1$s is no longer in the library folder.
%1$s is prepared: import it to play.
%1$s is running: playing this game closes it (saves are kept).
%1$s is running and will close. Press Play again within 5 seconds.
A folder holding several games: disc images and extracted folders. The app lists them; you import the ones you play.

With All files access the app reads your library folder as it is: extracted game folders play in place, disc images are read without copying. Without it, Android\'s file picker still lets the app list the folder, but every game must be imported or copied.
Without All files access: games are listed, then imported or copied into the app
The copy the app made when importing the game. Deleting it frees the space; the game stays in the library and can be imported again. Your disc image or folder is never touched.

The game is read straight from your disc image, where it is: nothing was copied or extracted. The app keeps only the image\'s XBE files (for the title, the art and the Prepare). Deleting forgets the image; the image itself is never touched.
What the Prepare built for this game. Once deleted, the game needs preparing again (20 to 60 minutes).
The Prepare\'s work files (generated code, objects). Only needed to resume or redo a Prepare faster.
The game\'s own caches (Z:, the cache partitions, E:\\CACHE), kept aside while another game plays. The game rebuilds them at its next start, which can take a few minutes.
Your saved games for this title. Deleted saves cannot be recovered.
Press A again within 5 seconds to delete it.
Your saves will be lost for good. Press A again within 5 seconds to delete them.
Only what the app made is deleted here: never your disc images nor the folders of your library folder.
Saves are only deleted from here, one game at a time: nothing else deletes them.
Not prepared · plays in the interpreter
Prepared · %1$d new addresses found · prepare again
Play starts the game at once, in the interpreter. Prepare translates it for this device (a few minutes) so that it runs natively; you can play meanwhile.
The game runs from its preparation. Code it does not cover still runs in the interpreter and is noted for the next Prepare.
This update translates games better. Prepare again to get its fixes; until then the game plays as before. Your saves are kept.
Your last games ran code the preparation had missed (%1$d addresses). Prepare again to translate it too; Play works meanwhile.
The preparation failed (%1$s); the game still plays in the interpreter. See what failed for the log.
%1$s is prepared: it now runs natively.
Play starts the game from its disc, through the PlayStation BIOS the app carries (OpenBIOS).

Play starts the game from its cartridge file, no BIOS needed. Saves and the controller pak are kept for each game. The second button puts a rumble pak in the controller instead (no controller pak saves then).

Play starts the game at once from its cartridge file, in the interpreter. Prepare translates it for this device (a few minutes) so that it runs natively; you can play meanwhile. The last button picks the controller pak (saves) or a rumble pak.
Play starts the game from its cartridge file, no BIOS needed. A rumble pak is in the controller: your pad vibrates when the game says so. The second button puts the controller pak back (its saves).
%1$s is a favourite: first in the library
No game matches « %1$s ». B clears the search.
No game of this console. L1 / R1 change the console.
